note: Orders every 2 days (even days) at 110% of the forecast for the next two arrival days, which balances the 39 order fee against holding cost; risk: the 30% demand noise causes shortages between deliveries.
Daily orders at 108% of forecast keep stock low; risk: 25 order fees of 39 each (975) cost more than the holding they save.
Orders every 3 days at 110% of forecast; risk: high holding cost for product 1 (0.7 per day) and arrivals near the 176 warehouse limit.
Orders every 2 days at exactly the forecast; risk: actual demand averages about 4.6% above forecast, so there is no safety stock and shortage penalties pile up.
Orders every 2 days at 120% of forecast for a high fill rate; risk: extra holding cost, unsold stock at the end, and arrivals near capacity on day 15.
Orders every 2 days with asymmetric safety stock (105% for product 0, 115% for the higher-margin product 1); risk: product 0 runs short more often.
Orders every 2 days on odd days, plus a day-0 order for day 5, at 110% of forecast; risk: one extra order fee and a slightly worse fit to the demand peaks.
Daily orders at 125% of forecast, so almost no shortages; risk: both the order fees and the holding cost and write-offs from overstock are high.
